title: AI-lab chronology - focus shifts, capability milestones, and the EA / Open-Philanthropy / safety-reg-arbitrage pathways
source: Public record: lab histories + timelines; Open Philanthropy / SFF / FLI grant records; SB 1047 + the 2026 pacing fight (see spec-buist-v-anthropic-pacing). Chronology overlay (structural; no financial-core edges; dollar figures in notes). TAXONOMY NOTE: 'AI' spans symbolic AI, expert systems, ML, RL, computer vision, protein folding, robotics, etc. - LLMs (transformer language models, 2017+) are ONE recently-dominant BRANCH, not AI itself; this block keeps that distinction. HONESTY: grants/dates/milestones = fact (amounts as reported); influence + 'regulatory arbitrage' framing = interpretation, labeled.

edges.notes: 2017: Open Philanthropy granted OpenAI ~$30M and took a board seat (Holden Karnofsky) - the earliest EA-money-into-a-frontier-lab pathway, justified as buying safety influence over capability (fact; influence-vs-capture framing interpretation).
Open Philanthropy (Dustin Moskovitz + Cari Tuna) is the largest EA grantmaker - the hub routing EA capital into AI-safety orgs, policy shops, and labs (fact).

Anthropic (founded 2021 by ex-OpenAI staff incl. the Amodei siblings) was built with heavy EA/AI-safety framing; early capital included ~$500M tied to FTX/SBF (later part of the FTX bankruptcy estate) - the EA-to-frontier-lab pattern at its clearest (fact of founding + FTX stake; motive framing interpretation).

SFF (Jaan Tallinn's recommendation-driven fund) + FLI + Longview channel money into the AI-safety-POLICY ecosystem (Encode, safety think tanks) - the funding rail behind the pacing/pause-letter apparatus mapped in spec-buist-v-anthropic-pacing (fact of funding; influence interpretation).
Encode co-sponsored California's SB 1047 (2024 frontier-AI safety bill) - the youth-safety-advocacy vehicle at the center of the safety-legislation push (fact).

SB 1047 (2024) - mandatory frontier-model safety testing + kill-switch + liability - passed the CA legislature and was VETOED by Gov. Newsom (Sep 2024); the template + battleground for the 2025-26 state-vs-federal AI-safety-regulation fight (fact).

Anthropic has positioned as the safety-forward lab that (selectively) SUPPORTS regulation - the 'pacing' posture that critics recode as regulatory arbitrage (raise rivals' compliance cost, entrench incumbents); see the 2026 pacing-as-cartel fight (fact of positioning; arbitrage framing = interpretation/contested).

OpenAI's stance shifted from 'we won't wait for an exemption' toward selective regulation-shaping; the labs' collective push to 'build the brake' rather than pull it is the core of the safety-regulatory-arbitrage debate (fact of statements; framing interpretation).

TAXONOMY ANCHOR: DeepMind's landmark wins were NON-LLM AI - AlphaGo (2016, deep RL + tree search) and AlphaFold (2020-24, protein structure, a Nobel) - a reminder that 'AI' is not 'LLM'; the safety-reg debate now centers on LLMs but the field + the risks are broader (fact; taxonomy point).
